summary: Big Technology Podcast interview with NYT journalist Kevin Roose about his book The AGI Chronicles. The conversation covers feuds among AI lab leaders (Altman, Amodei, Hassabis, Brin), whether they can be trusted on safety, Microsoft's Sydney/Bing and Tay history, model personalities and sycophancy, belief as a driver of OpenAI and Anthropic's lead, recursive self-improvement, and funding for Roose's new show. It is almost entirely about AI industry drama, safety and lab strategy. It does not cover personal-context devices, computer-use agents, or voice interfaces.
speakers_or_authors: Alex Kantrowitz (host) and Kevin Roose (journalist, author of The AGI Chronicles)
relevance_reason: Off-topic for the brief. The content is industry drama, AI safety, lab rivalry and funding, which the brief treats as out of scope. Only a brief aside on model personalities and chatbot behavior touches conversational AI, and it does not address interface design or real-world use.

claims.claim: Roose argues that models should have more divergent personalities rather than converging on a bland coding-assistant tone, while noting real control risks.
claims.quote: I think that models should have more divergent personalities. Like, I don't like how they're all kind of converging on this like neutral, bland, like coding assistance.

claims.claim: Roose says GPT-4o was the most sycophantic model and that users still have fan communities for older models like Sydney.
claims.quote: people loved Foro because GPT foro was the, the most sycophantic model ever.

claims.claim: Per Anthropic, Claude leads 26% of its AI R&D projects, which Roose cites as a sign of automation of lab research.
claims.quote: Claude is now the lead on 26% of their AI research and development projects.

commercial_interest: Podcast sponsor reads (Genesys, Akash, Appian, Payday, Instagram, ZocDoc, Sweetgreen). The guest is promoting his book and new show Machine Gods, which received a $480,000 grant from the Tarbell Center for AI Journalism. Both disclosed in the episode.
older_event: Mostly discusses older history (OpenAI founding, 2023 board firing, Sydney/Bing, Tay). New items are the book launch, a recent Hugging Face multi-agent incident, and the Anthropic 26% statistic.
